title: Drug Interactions: What You Should Know
supports: Different OTC products may share active ingredients; read all ingredients and ask a pharmacist or doctor about questions. Fictional X/Y diagrams are original educational examples, not real product claims.

title: How to Understand and Use the Nutrition Facts Label
supports: Serving size is not a recommendation; nutrient amounts scale with servings consumed. US label guidance, not an Indian label-format specification. 30 g / 12 g / 60 g are invented teaching numbers.

title: MATCH Toolkit, Chapter 3: Designing the Medication Reconciliation Process
supports: Verify medication information with patients and other sources, retain source/time information, and clarify discrepancies professionally. Reminder versus intake distinction is an educational application, not a quotation or dosing protocol.

title: Poisoning
supports: Seek immediate medical advice for suspected poisoning. Lesson says urgent local help rather than exporting UK phone numbers to other locations.

title: What Is Diabetes?
supports: Pancreas produces insulin; insulin helps glucose enter cells; type 2 can involve insufficient insulin and reduced response. Original schematic, not agency artwork or endorsement.

title: Your Digestive System & How It Works
supports: Carbohydrates break into simple sugars; the small intestine absorbs nutrients; the liver processes and supplies nutrients.

title: Insulin Resistance & Prediabetes
supports: Muscle, fat and liver cells may not respond well to insulin; the pancreas may not make enough to compensate. Not an individualized assessment.
